scope: Read-only inspection of installed official sandbox sources and a one-off pure environment-builder observation; no main harness/collector/algorithm/runtime file changed.
actual_manager_constructor_signature: (self, timeout_seconds: 'int' = 300, base_dir: 'Path | None' = None, system_site_packages: 'bool' = True)

findings.fresh_process: SubprocessManager.exec calls execute_subprocess_command for each call; helper uses a new subprocess.Popen and start_new_session=True, then kills process group on completion. Our heredoc python commands are separate processes, not a shared imported-module kernel.
findings.environment: Manager passes only VIRTUAL_ENV/PATH/PYTHONPATH in extra_env. Builder imports only _SAFE_ENV_KEYS from host and that allowlist excludes PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE/PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX. Setting host env alone is therefore dropped. Builder supports explicit extra_env, but Manager.exec has no caller env argument.
findings.source_initialization: Collector prepare_workspace already excludes __pycache__, .venv, venv and other excluded parts; source_inventory also excludes caches. stop removes the whole sandbox root, explaining unavailable original mtime/pyc header.
findings.prospective_policy: If root chooses a new runtime profile, use a collector-scoped, explicitly recorded manager env adaptation to inject PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 into the effective extra_env for every repository subprocess in phaseA/baseline/repaired. Materialize/copy workspace, then remove only workspace-local bytecode before any source preload/command, and prevent later writes. Preserve immutable dependency profiles. Do not silently claim current Manager already exposes env configuration.
findings.B_limit: -B/sys.dont_write_bytecode prevents writes, not reads of an already valid pyc. Initial source cache cleanliness is jointly required.
findings.non_target: This policy does not reload modules in an already-running Python process or invalidate live object references; same-process import/reload semantics remain a separate case.
